skill.name: lark-whiteboard
skill.description: Create Lark and Feishu whiteboard diagrams from user requests, including architecture diagrams, flowcharts, mind maps, org charts, funnels, pyramids, fishbone diagrams, and Mermaid-based diagrams.
skill.summary: Generate structured diagrams for Lark whiteboards and render or upload them with LarkSuite tools.
skill.author: larksuite

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, Mermaid examples, JavaScript template literals, relative documentation links, and high-density Chinese documentation. Confirmed risk remains because the skill intentionally runs npm, npx, node, and lark-cli commands, including authenticated Lark document and whiteboard updates. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before npm, npx, node, or lark-cli commands, and pin or verify the Lark whiteboard CLI package before execution.

remediation.issue: Authenticated Lark whiteboard updates can overwrite existing content
remediation.suggestion: Always perform the dry-run overwrite check, parse the deletion count, and require explicit user confirmation before removing dry-run or using overwrite.

remediation.issue: Generated scripts write local diagram artifacts
remediation.suggestion: Use a skill-scoped output directory with unique filenames, and do not allow user-controlled output paths in generated scripts.

remediation.issue: Relative links point outside the skill directory
remediation.suggestion: Replace ../ documentation references with packaged dependencies or marketplace dependency metadata so agents do not need to leave the skill boundary.

semantic_findings.description: The skill directs agents to upload generated content to existing Lark whiteboards and explains that nonempty boards may be cleared. The dry-run requirement is a mitigation, but a missed confirmation can delete user diagrams.

content.value_statement: Teams need clear diagrams in Lark documents without manually arranging every shape. This skill plans, generates, renders, and can upload whiteboard diagrams using LarkSuite tooling.
actual_capabilities: Routes requests between a structured whiteboard DSL path and a Mermaid path.
Provides layout rules for architecture, organization, comparison, fishbone, funnel, pyramid, flywheel, and milestone diagrams.
Defines whiteboard node schemas, connector rules, typography guidance, and color palettes.
Uses generated JSON or Mermaid files as input for the Lark whiteboard CLI renderer.
Includes upload guidance for Lark documents and whiteboards through lark-cli with dry-run checks.
limitations: Requires Node.js 18 or later and LarkSuite command line tools.
Uploading to Lark requires valid authentication and document permissions.
Complex layouts may need render review and iterative adjustment.
The output targets Lark whiteboards, not general web or presentation design tools.

use_cases.description: Build org charts, comparison views, and planning diagrams that can be rendered and shared in Lark documents.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Diagram
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner wants one simple board.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a simple Lark whiteboard architecture diagram for a web app with frontend, API, database, and cache layers.

prompt_templates.title: Process Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: A user needs a Mermaid-friendly workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Lark whiteboard flowchart for an order approval process with submit, review, approve, reject, and notify steps.

prompt_templates.scenario: A team wants a specific diagram type.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a fishbone diagram for delayed product releases with causes grouped by planning, engineering, testing, dependencies, and communication.

prompt_templates.title: Render And Upload
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user has Lark access and wants delivery into a document.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create, render, review, and upload a Lark whiteboard funnel diagram to my existing board token after running the required dry-run overwrite check.

output_examples.input: Create a microservice architecture diagram for checkout.
output_examples.output: A layered whiteboard diagram with user, gateway, service, messaging, storage, and observability groups, using consistent colors and labeled connectors.

output_examples.input: Make a sales funnel diagram for website conversion.
output_examples.output: A funnel board with stages for visits, signups, trials, opportunities, and purchases, with decreasing widths and readable stage labels.

output_examples.input: Draw an org chart for a small product team.
output_examples.output: A hierarchical whiteboard with leadership, product, design, engineering, and QA nodes, plus right-angle connectors between levels.

best_practices: Start with the diagram goal, audience, and required chart type before choosing Mermaid or DSL.
Render and inspect the PNG before uploading to Lark.
Run the dry-run overwrite check and ask for explicit confirmation before updating an existing board.
anti_patterns: Do not upload to an existing whiteboard without checking whether it contains nodes.
Do not use long paragraphs inside diagram nodes.
Do not hand-place complex absolute coordinates when the scene guide requires script generation.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates diagrams for Lark and Feishu whiteboards, including architecture diagrams, flows, org charts, funnels, pyramids, and Mermaid diagrams.

faq.question: Does it require Lark authentication?
faq.answer: Rendering local images does not require Lark authentication. Uploading to a Lark document or whiteboard requires valid credentials and permissions.

faq.question: Can it use Mermaid?
faq.answer: Yes. It routes mind maps, sequence diagrams, class diagrams, pie charts, and flowcharts to Mermaid when that path is appropriate.

faq.question: Can it update an existing whiteboard?
faq.answer: Yes, but the skill requires a dry-run check first. The user must confirm before any overwrite can proceed.

faq.question: What tools does it need?
faq.answer: It needs Node.js 18 or later, the Lark whiteboard CLI, and lark-cli for authenticated Lark document operations.

faq.question: Is it safe to auto-install?
faq.answer: Auto-install should require confirmation because the skill can run npx, npm, node scripts, and authenticated lark-cli commands.
